findings.obligation: L3/F111 as the design states it: a resume keeps a subset of the plan it resumes, in plan order, each position at most once, so a plan never grows from one run to the next.
findings.observation: Non-blocking. The reworked binding reads verdict.to_read and verdict.skipped, so the property is asserted over the repos read now and the repos given up on. The kept plan the resuming run actually writes is Resume::kept(), which is to_read plus carried (crates/review-domain/src/repo_scope/resume.rs:96) and is what the scan task maps at crates/openlore-review-app/src/scan.rs:608. The carried share is now observed nowhere: grep over tests/, crates/review-domain and crates/openlore-review-app/src finds .carried and kept() only in production, and the existing domain property at tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_and_accounts_core.rs:370 reads to_read and skipped too. Both journeys pass their account checks, so carried is empty in them. A carried position outside the plan, repeated, or out of order would therefore not be caught, although the declared law is about exactly that set. Craft is not invalidated: P1 and P2 keep public falsifiers in the two journeys and in L2.
findings.remediation: Either add verdict.carried to the accounted positions in sut_picked_up - one line, over a field this design leaves in place - so the property covers the kept set the resuming run writes; or, if the shape of carried under the declared KeptRow change is uncertain, say so in the manifest as an explicit coverage limitation of L3/F111 instead of leaving the carried rows silently unobserved.

No proptest regression file was written; git status --porcelain stayed empty.

The twice-paused journey is the public falsifier the one-pause journey could not be. Printed evidence: her paused run read priyaraman/tidepool, the first pick-up read priyaraman/quill-docs, the second read priyaraman/kelp, the run is stored completed, and her queue status region reads '1 repo read'. Each run read a repo none of the others read, so the three she chose were read once between them, and the count falls back to the last run's single read. This is semantic RED at the public HTTP port for L1/F101 and L4/F115 as the manifest now binds them, and it discriminates exactly the behaviour the previous one-pause journey admitted it could not (a count right after one pause that falls back after a second).

No test now answers its own assertion. sut_picked_up reads only verdict.to_read and verdict.skipped, two answers this design leaves in place, and nothing in the file opens the store: the KeptRepo.carries_an_earlier_read literal, TakenOver, StoredRepo, sut_freeze_plan and sut_frozen_plan are gone with the three store-direct tests. L2 now computes the already-read positions from the generated plan alone and intersects them with to_read, so it is falsifiable on production: resume_plan filters status == Planned (crates/review-domain/src/repo_scope/resume.rs:131), and the generator always inserts an already-read row whose account passes its check, so dropping that filter puts that position into to_read and the property goes red. Derived by reading the bytes; no production source was modified to confirm it.

Reuse of the unchanged companion checks, justified by the comparison above rather than re-executed. adapter-review-store, review-domain, xtask and the review-app supports are byte-identical between ca0db1f and a3d69f9, so the results recorded for ca0db1f stand: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_scan_store_failure exit 0, 4 passed; cargo test -p review-domain -p adapter-review-store exit 0, 220 passed, among them scan_runs::tests::a_purge_between_scan_start_and_plan_write_leaves_no_rows ... ok, which the manifest now binds to L4/F117; cargo xtask check-arch exit 0 for T1. The adapter round trip for row identity and order is no longer asserted here; the 104 passing in-crate adapter tests own it and the journeys falsify the status-carrying claim end to end, so nothing promised to the owner is left unobserved.

diagnostic: Accepted. The three rejecting findings are resolved in the delta and were removed. The fabricated carries_an_earlier_read literal, the status-dropping store writer binding and the three store-direct L4 tests are gone; the single remaining binding, sut_picked_up, reads only verdict.to_read and verdict.skipped, two answers this design leaves in place, so no line of it has to move when the verdict starts naming the repos already read and the crafter never needs to touch this file. Exact carrying is now observed where the owner can see it: the new twice-paused journey drives the real binary over HTTP and reads '1 repo read' against the three repos the three runs read between them (left 1, right 3), beside the one-pause journey's '2 repos read' (left 2, right 3). Both failures are the missing production behaviour, both go green exactly when a run picking a plan up takes over the reads that plan holds, and the second one discriminates the fallback the first admitted it could not. L2 is no longer pass-for-free: it computes the already-read positions from the generated plan alone, and resume_plan's status == Planned filter is what keeps it green. L4/F117 is bound to the existing passing adapter test instead of a duplicate, and L4/F115 and L4/F116 are bound to the journeys that falsify them end to end. One non-blocking finding stays open for the oracle owner: L3's observation no longer covers the carried share of the kept plan, which nothing else observes either. Companion checks are reused on byte-identical inputs, not re-executed, and are cited as such. typesafe: unavailable (key absent), so every judgment is locally derived. No design, implementation or product finding; craft may proceed on this oracle, with the two journeys' GREEN and the live count remaining completion obligations.
